newsitem.title: USA: CSX Corp sees another strong year in '97.
newsitem.headline: CSX Corp sees another strong year in '97.

text.p: CSX Corp said Thursday it expects another strong year, based on record first quarter results. The company reported first-quarter earnings of $151 million, or $0.70 cents per share.

CSX said it expects the economy will continue to show moderate growth, increasing transportation demand. And through the balance of the year, said CSX, it will stress fundamental improvements at all its businesses, especially focusing on service to customers and cost controls.

The company said rail earnings were very strong in the quarter, more than offsetting the effects of rate pressures in key ocean container trade lanes and extreme flooding conditions on the inland waterways that hurt Sea-Land, its barge company.

CSX added that its core rail business posted a record first quarter operating ratio of 77.4 percent, almost three points lower than the prior year's quarter and two points below the prior record achieved in 1995's first quarter.
"This gives us a great head start on the year," said John Snow, chairman and chief executive.
CSX provides rail, container-shipping, intermodal, trucking, barge and contract logistics services.
